newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GENCOR TO LIST IN LONDON, RAISE $1 BLN.
newsitem.headline: GENCOR TO LIST IN LONDON, RAISE $1 BLN.

text.p: South African mining house Gencor Ltd said on Wednesday it planned to list its non-precious metals operations as a new company, Billiton Plc, in London, and raise $1 billion in Britain, the U.S. and Europe.

"Billiton will be one of the largest and lowest cost producers of aluminium and the leading producer of ferroalloys, the world's largest exporter of thermal coal and a leading source of titanium minerals," the company said in a statement.

Gencor chairman Brian Gilbertson said Billiton would be able to raise far larger sums in London than it could from a South African base. He said the proposed deal had already been approved by the South African Reserve Bank.
"There is no model of gold mining leadership within a diversified commodity portfolio and Gencor management felt it was essential to focus the two different business," said Gilbertson.

The transfer of Gencor's non-precious metals interests to the Billiton company would be effected through the issue of three Billiton shares and one letter of entitlement for every four Gencor shares held by existing Gencor shareholders.

Gencor directors Mick Davis, Dave Munro and Mike Salamon would resign in August to devote themselves fully to Billiton. Gilbertson, who will be executive chairman of Billiton, would continue as chairman of Gencor "for the time being".
Mick Davis will become Billiton's executive director finance, coal and human resources.
Gilbertson said the previously announced merger of Gencor's nickel interests with those of Australian producer QNI Ltd would be Billiton's first transaction.
The company said Billiton would also seek a secondary listing on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, while it expected to qualify for admission to the FT-SE 100 Index when it listed in London.
Billiton's pro-forma attributable profit for the nine months to March 1997 was U.S.$417 million, nearly equalling its attributable profit for the whole of 1996 of U.S.$433 million.

"The new Gencor will define a new mission to achieve a place among the world's leading gold producers, measured by output, by cost of production and by market value. It will not diversify outside of precious metals," Gilbertson said.

Gencor's major assets include Beatrix Mines Ltd , the lowest cost-producer in the world, Oryx Gold Holdings Ltd and St Helena Gold Mines Ltd in the southern Free State province, Evander Gold Mines Ltd in Mpumalanga province and Impala Platinum Holdings Ltd .
Billiton's major assets will be Gencor's holding in Billiton, Samancor Ltd , Alusaf, Richards Bay Minerals, Ingwe Coal Corp and its nickel interests.
